# fileconfig

```go
import "gorontalo/pkg/fileconfig"
```

Package fileconfig reads a single configuration file from disk and decodes it into a caller\-chosen type.

It targets the common case: one known file, decoded once into one typed struct. It deliberately does not do what Viper does — environment and flag merging, remote stores, live reloading, case\-insensitive key lookup. For that one\-file case the standard library is enough, so this package pulls in no third\-party dependencies: os.ReadFile plus encoding/json by default. The decoder is pluggable \(Config.Decoder\), so a caller that needs YAML can supply one without every other caller taking on that dependency.

The type to decode into is a generic parameter, so Load returns a \*T with no casting:

```
type AppConfig struct {
    Addr string `json:"addr"`
    Port int    `json:"port"`
}

loader, err := fileconfig.New(fileconfig.Config[AppConfig]{
    Path: "configs/app.json",
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
cfg, err := loader.Load(ctx)
```

A relative Path is resolved against the process working directory \(the app root\), so "configs/app.json" refers to \<root\>/configs/app.json. An absolute Path is used as\-is.

Caching is controlled by TTL and CachePermanently. The zero value of both disables caching: every Load re\-reads and re\-decodes the file. A positive TTL caches a successful result for that duration, after which the next Load re\-reads. CachePermanently reads the file once on the first Load and returns that value for every later Load, overriding TTL. The context passed to Load bounds each actual read, so a caller can cancel or set a deadline independently.

Validation is optional. When Config.Validate is set it runs on the decoded value and its error is surfaced to the caller; when it is nil the only decode\-time error a caller sees is the underlying unmarshal error.

Errors are returned as \*stderr.StdErr so they carry an application error code and an HTTP status at the service boundary.

### Usage

```
loader, err := fileconfig.New(fileconfig.Config[AppConfig]{
    Path: "configs/app.json",
    TTL:  2 * time.Second,
    Validate: func(c *AppConfig) error {
        if c.Port <= 0 {
            return errors.New("port must be positive")
        }
        return nil
    },
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
cfg, err := loader.Load(ctx)
```

The zero value of Loader is not usable; create one with New.

## Constants

<a name="CodeInvalidConfig"></a>Error codes reported on the \*stderr.StdErr returned by New and Load.

```go
const (
    // CodeInvalidConfig means the Config passed to New was unusable (e.g. an
    // empty Path).
    CodeInvalidConfig = "FILECONFIG_INVALID_CONFIG"

    // CodeReadFailed means the file could not be read (missing, no permission,
    // or the read timed out / was canceled).
    CodeReadFailed = "FILECONFIG_READ_FAILED"

    // CodeDecodeFailed means the file contents could not be decoded into T.
    CodeDecodeFailed = "FILECONFIG_DECODE_FAILED"

    // CodeValidationFailed means the decoded value failed Config.Validate.
    CodeValidationFailed = "FILECONFIG_VALIDATION_FAILED"
)
```

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/xwinata/gorontalo/blob/main/pkg/fileconfig/options.go#L12-L39>)

Config customizes a Loader created by New. Only Path is required; every other field has a usable zero value.

```go
type Config[T any] struct {
    // Path is the configuration file to read. A relative path is resolved
    // against the process working directory (the app root); an absolute path is
    // used as-is. Required: an empty Path makes New fail.
    Path string

    // TTL is how long a successfully loaded value is cached and reused before
    // Load re-reads the file. Zero (the default) disables caching: every Load
    // re-reads and re-decodes the file. A positive TTL caches the value for
    // that duration, after which the next Load re-reads. A negative value is
    // treated as zero. Ignored when CachePermanently is set.
    TTL time.Duration

    // CachePermanently, when true, reads the file once on the first Load and
    // returns that cached value for every later Load. It overrides TTL.
    CachePermanently bool

    // Decoder decodes the raw file bytes into *T. When nil, encoding/json is
    // used. Supply a YAML (or other) decoder here to read other formats without
    // this package depending on them.
    Decoder func(data []byte, v any) error

    // Validate, when non-nil, checks the decoded value after a successful
    // decode. A non-nil error it returns is surfaced to the Load caller wrapped
    // with CodeValidationFailed. When nil, the only decode-stage error a caller
    // sees is the underlying unmarshal error (wrapped with CodeDecodeFailed).
    Validate func(*T) error
}
```

<a name="Loader"></a>
## type [Loader](<https://github.com/xwinata/gorontalo/blob/main/pkg/fileconfig/fileconfig.go#L101-L107>)

Loader reads and decodes a configuration file into a \*T. It is safe for concurrent use. By default \(zero TTL, CachePermanently false\) every Load re\-reads the file; a positive Config.TTL caches a result for that duration, and Config.CachePermanently caches the first result forever. Create one with New.

```go
type Loader[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/xwinata/gorontalo/blob/main/pkg/fileconfig/fileconfig.go#L114>)

```go
func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) (*Loader[T], error)
```

New validates cfg and returns a Loader that decodes into T. It fails with a \*stderr.StdErr carrying CodeInvalidConfig when Path is empty. All other fields have valid zero values: a zero TTL with CachePermanently false disables caching, a nil Decoder selects JSON, and a nil Validate skips validation.

<a name="Loader[T].Load"></a>
### func \(\*Loader\[T\]\) [Load](<https://github.com/xwinata/gorontalo/blob/main/pkg/fileconfig/fileconfig.go#L136>)

```go
func (l *Loader[T]) Load(ctx context.Context) (*T, error)
```

Load returns the configured value, decoded into a new T.

Caching depends on Config: with the default \(zero TTL, CachePermanently false\) every call re\-reads the file. A positive TTL serves a cached copy until the TTL elapses; CachePermanently serves the first result for every later call. A cache hit returns a copy of the cached value without touching the disk; otherwise Load reads the file, decodes it into a new T, runs the optional validator, caches the result when caching is enabled, and returns it.

Each actual read is bounded by ctx. On any failure it returns a \*stderr.StdErr whose code identifies the stage that failed \(CodeReadFailed, CodeDecodeFailed, or CodeValidationFailed\); a failed Load leaves any existing cached value untouched.
